title: Literal checks until the skill is modelled
statement: Until a skill has been modelled, checks on the reading ask only what the text states; independent use of the skill comes after the model.
example: Checks on pages 6 to 12 stayed literal because inference was first modelled on page 19, and independent inference was then asked four times.
detail: An external audit of a Grade 3 lesson found that all eight reading checks during the story were literal retrieval, with inference only inside guided steps. The ruling kept them literal: they come before the worked model of inference, so an independent inference item there would break the gradual-release order, and the lesson asks for independent inference four times after its independent step. A later review listed the retrieval-only checks in four lessons for a last look that none reads as a 'why do you think' question.
against: The audit's verdict was "Reasoning happens, but the method never lets go of the student's hand" (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-inceptbench-2026-09-18/REGISTER.md`, line 12), and the same row notes that keeping the checks literal also kept the lesson in the shape of an earlier lesson in the course.
